Variable Font Technology

A typeface built to fit the reader.

This is technology in its most direct form: built around how people actually read, not how a grid wants them to. Lexend — the reading-fluency typeface Thomas co-created with Dr. Bonnie Shaver-Troup — has been downloaded more than 500,000 times through Google Fonts and rendered on over 2 billion webviews. Readex is its open-source, world-script expansion.

Thought Leadership

τὸ καλόν

The judgment beauty still requires.

Technology can generate endless options; it still takes a human to decide which one is worth wanting. A blind study of 20 designers found human-made typographic work beat AI-generated work 8 times out of 9 in head-to-head comparison — not because AI can’t produce visually interesting layouts, but because it couldn’t reliably honor the constraints the work actually required. That gap is the same gap Plato and Aristotle pointed to with to kalon: beauty as the thing that makes a claim on you, rather than the thing that’s merely on offer. Making technology serve beauty, instead of replacing the judgment beauty requires, is the argument the book makes in full.

Third Spaces

Typography culture that never needed a classroom.

Most of this work now happens through software, screens, and increasingly AI. TypeThursday is the deliberate counterweight — it started as a handful of people meeting in a Brooklyn bar to critique letterforms, and has since grown into a global, chapter-based community that still meets in person, monthly, city by city, because judgment sharpens in conversation, not in isolation.
